    SCT Interface

    Source: vignettes/sct-interface.Rmd
    sct-interface.Rmd

    Overview

    scimagR provides R wrappers for the Spinal Cord Toolbox (SCT) command-line tools. The code in this vignette is not run when the vignette is built, because it needs SCT and your own images. The wrappers handle:

    • Path resolution (respects the SCT_DIR environment variable)
    • The command syntax of the installed SCT version: SCT 7.0 replaced sct_deepseg -task <task> with sct_deepseg <task> and renamed the tasks; the wrappers read the version from sct_version and use the matching form
    • Input validation
    • Idempotent execution (skip if the output exists)
    • Structured error reporting: a failed command gives a warning with the end of its error output, and the wrapper returns NA; so does a command that exits normally without writing the expected file
    • Optional QC report generation

    Configuration

    Set the SCT_DIR environment variable if SCT is not on your PATH:

    Sys.setenv(SCT_DIR = "/path/to/sct")

    Or add it to your .Renviron:

    SCT_DIR=/path/to/sct

    Spinal Cord Segmentation

    The contrast-agnostic model (sct_deepseg spinalcord):

    library(scimagR)

sc_seg <- sct_segment_sc(
  input = "sub-01_T2w.nii.gz",
  qc_dir = "qc/"
)
# "sub-01_T2w_seg.nii.gz"

    Lesion Segmentation (SCIsegV2)

    SCIsegV2 (sct_deepseg lesion_sci_t2) segments the lesion and the spinal cord. The lesion mask is returned; the cord mask is saved next to it as *_sc_seg.nii.gz:

    lesion_seg <- sct_segment_lesion(
  input = "sub-01_T2w.nii.gz",
  qc_dir = "qc/"
)
# "sub-01_T2w_lesion_seg.nii.gz" (and "sub-01_T2w_sc_seg.nii.gz")

    Vertebral Labelling

    sct_label_vertebrae names its outputs after the segmentation. The wrapper returns the labelled segmentation (*_seg_labeled.nii.gz), the file that sct_process_segmentation() needs; the disc labels are written next to it (*_seg_labeled_discs.nii.gz).

    vert_labels <- sct_label_vertebrae(
  input = "sub-01_T2w.nii.gz",
  segmentation = sc_seg
)
# "sub-01_T2w_seg_labeled.nii.gz"

    Parameter Extraction 

    # Lesion parameters (volume, length, tissue bridges): an Excel spreadsheet,
# *_analysis.xlsx (*_analysis.xls with SCT 6.4)
lesion_xlsx <- sct_analyze_lesion(
  lesion_seg = lesion_seg,
  sc_seg = "sub-01_T2w_sc_seg.nii.gz"
)

# Morphometric parameters (CSA, diameters), averaged over C2-C7 and
# reported per vertebral level
csa_csv <- sct_process_segmentation(
  sc_seg = sc_seg,
  vert_labels = vert_labels,
  vert = 2:7,
  perlevel = TRUE
)

    Without vert, sct_process_segmentation() averages the metrics over all slices of the segmentation, and the VertLevel column of the CSV is empty.

    QC Reports

    The segmentation wrappers write QC reports when given qc_dir. To make a report afterwards, use sct_generate_qc():

    # Spinal cord segmentation
sct_generate_qc(
  input = "sub-01_T2w.nii.gz",
  segmentation = sc_seg,
  qc_dir = "qc/"
)

# Lesion: the cord mask as `segmentation`, the lesion mask as `lesion`
sct_generate_qc(
  input = "sub-01_T2w.nii.gz",
  segmentation = "sub-01_T2w_sc_seg.nii.gz",
  lesion = lesion_seg,
  qc_dir = "qc/",
  process = "sct_deepseg_lesion",
  plane = "sagittal"
)

    Idempotent Execution

    All SCT wrappers that write images are idempotent by default. If the output file already exists, the function returns the existing path without re-running:

    # First call: runs segmentation
sct_segment_sc("sub-01_T2w.nii.gz")

# Second call: skips, returns existing path
sct_segment_sc("sub-01_T2w.nii.gz")

# Force re-run:
sct_segment_sc("sub-01_T2w.nii.gz", overwrite = TRUE)

    Troubleshooting

    Common issues:

    • “Cannot find sct_deepseg on PATH”: Set SCT_DIR or add SCT bin/ to PATH
    • A wrapper returns NA: read the warning; it shows the exit code and the last lines of the SCT error output, or names the output file SCT did not write
    • Python errors: Ensure the correct Python environment is activated
